title: Ordering gate telemetry sequencer for async span flushes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: client SDKs and edge workers sometimes emit spans and partial request traces asynchronously. Under load or when retries/queues are involved, related spans can arrive out of order at the ingestion pipeline, causing incorrect parent-child relationships, misleading latency histograms, and poor error attribution. This is most visible for long-tail asynchronous request patterns (webhooks, background jobs, streaming chunk flushes) and for mobile/offline SDKs that buffer and flush when connectivity returns.\n\nProposal: implement a lightweight ordering gate ("telemetry sequencer") consisting of two cooperating pieces: (1) a client/SDK library header that tags spans with a compact provenance epoch and a per-callseq monotonic sequence id (two 64-bit-ish fields packed to minimize overhead), and (2) an ingestion-side reordering buffer that accepts out-of-order spans for a configurable, short window and emits them in sequence to the downstream assembler. The sequencer is optional and enabled per-customer/route via flags. The design aims for small CPU and network overhead while materially reducing reassembly errors and incorrect latency spikes in dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: SDK: emit provenance_epoch and seq_id headers for request families with < 50ns median overhead in hot paths
Ingest: reordering buffer successfully reorders 99% of simulated out-of-order span sequences within a 200ms window
Dashboards: reduce 'invalid parent' trace artifacts in replayed workload by >= 80% for async patterns
Backwards compatible: spans without headers are passed through unchanged
Feature flag controls: support per-team opt-in and rollout stages in console
tasks: Design spec: finalize header encoding and wire format (Confluence doc)
SDK: implement header emission in Node/Python/Go SDKs behind flag
Agent: add lightweight sequencer stage to ingestion pipeline (configurable window)
Integration tests: fuzzed ordering/reorder-window experiments and perf microbenchmarks
Dashboard: add telemetry charts for reorder-rate, reorder-latency, and percent-ordered traces
Rollout: alpha -> beta customers -> progressive ramp to 100% with rollback plan
telemetry_queries: reorder_rate: count(span_received with header and seq_id where seq_id != expected) / count(spans_with_header)
reorder_latency: histogram(reorder_emit_time - first_arrival_time) by route, model
invalid_parent_reduction: compare historical invalid-parent-percent pre/post rollout
overhead_cpu_micro: p50 additional CPU ns/span in SDK hotpath
rollout_plan: 1) Feature behind tenant flag. 2) Internal alpha on staging with synthetic fuzz tests (2 days). 3) Beta with two customers and small production percentage (10%) for 1 week. 4) Monitor reorder_rate, reorder_latency, and error budgets; expand to 50% then 100% with 24h observation windows. 5) If reorder_latency causes tail regressions, immediately scale down window and fail open (pass-through) until root cause resolved.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Reordering buffer adds a bounded delay; must tune window per route to avoid tail regressions.
- Client header increases payload by a few bytes; must keep encoding compact and optionally compress in batched payloads.
- If clocks/ids diverge across clients, sequencer must rely only on per-family monotonic seq_id and epoch.
- Complexity in ingestion increases state; we mitigate with TTL-based eviction and metrics to detect build-up.
qa_plan: Unit tests for header encoder/decoder, property tests for monotonicity, fuzzing over packet loss and reorder patterns, load tests with synthetic producers to validate no memory blowup, and e2e tracing tests comparing assembled callgraphs with and without sequencer under identical synthetic scenarios.
notes: We evaluated purely server-side reconstruction using causal graph heuristics but found it delivers lower correctness for heavily fragmented flush patterns. The hybrid approach (small client tag + short server window) hit the best cost/correctness tradeoff in our benchmarks. Will document compatibility with existing sampling & baggage headers.
